channel.title: The Brand Identity – Features
channel.description: Graphic and brand design projects, interviews, and insights.

item.title: Omoi’s identity for Eclipse Space looks back to the Apollo programme
item.description: Eclipse Space designs and builds satellite constellations – groups of satellites working together in orbit – that nations, telcos and operators own outright. The people behind the company had designed, scaled and deployed ‘megaconstellations,’ the largest of these networks, before founding it. Stockholm-based creative studio Omoi was commissioned to create the company’s brand strategy, identity, website, 3D visuals, pitch deck and explainer film.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: How Molto Bureau designed the identity of a Saudi perfume house
item.description: Perfume Palace is a perfume house founded in Saudi Arabia that offers a twist on the region’s perfumery traditions by pairing classic Arabian notes with contemporary compositions. It approached Kyiv-based branding studio Molto Bureau to refresh its identity and packaging, spanning the logotype, label, brand materials and guidelines. The brand needed a cohesive rethinking of its visual language, with the update coming alongside a new batch of bottles. Over the years, the fragrances had built a loyal following, yet the identity no longer matched its quality, so the aim was to move Perfume Palace into a more premium register and give it a presence that would be recognisable, even on a crowded shelf.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Remembering Mitch Paone, the jazz pianist who coined kinetic identity
item.description: The late Mitch Paone, Co-founder & Creative Director of French Alps-based studio DIA, coined the term kinetic identity – an identity defined by how it behaves over time. A trained jazz pianist, he brought music into his classrooms, opening workshops at the keyboard and showing students how to set rules and improvise inside them. In this conversation, four close colleagues and friends remember him: ECAL’s Head of Graphic Design Angelo Benedetto, HEAD – Genève’s Head of MA Media Design Alexia Mathieu, ZHdK’s Head of BA Visual Communication Jonas Voegeli and KABK’s former Co-head of Graphic Design Roosje Klap. To Klap, Paone was “someone at the top of the field” and yet “more interested in your ideas than in his own.” His wife, Meg Donohoe, DIA’s Co-founder & Managing Director, reflects on the systems they built together, which “will keep running.” Mitch’s own words on design education appear throughout.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: How .raw reworked STOW’s identity to make its coffee roasting visible
item.description: Founded in 2015, STOW is a Slovenian speciality coffee company, with its roastery in Kamnik and cafés in Ljubljana. It brought in branding and marketing studio .raw to rework its existing look into an identity that would translate STOW’s scientific approach into visual form. “We reached a point where the work happening behind the scenes – the sourcing decisions, the roasting parameters, the testing – wasn’t visible in how the brand presented itself,” explains Peter Ševič from STOW. “We knew what we stood for, but the identity wasn’t carrying that across.”
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Fix Studio’s identity asks how to archive Puerto Rican visual culture
item.description: Instituto de Observación Colectiva (IOC) is an initiative that artist Christopher Gregory-Rivera founded in 2026 to support photography engaging with the histories of Puerto Rico and its diaspora, through fellowships, mentorship, workshops and public programming. Its first grant and mentorship programme is titled Counter Histories: Puerto Rico. Brooklyn-based Fix Studio, which had worked with Gregory-Rivera before, came on board from the start to create IOC’s identity and website. “While I had a strong idea of what the mission was, I did not have a clear idea of what that looked like,” Gregory-Rivera tells us.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: How the NeueHaus identity became a platform for its members’ work
item.description: NeueHaus is a membership-based network of creative professionals from the design and technology world, positioned as the “new creative guild.” Informed by the ideas and feedback of its members, the Büro – the studio behind the platform – relaunched NeueHaus’ identity across the website, app, social media and brand artefacts. The core team bringing it to life included Co-founder Alessandro Amato on design, motion and creative engineering, Co-founder Lena Pia Hammerstingl on creative direction and NeueHaus member Tom Mussak on art direction and design.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: How BonTemps© sequenced Sandy Ho’s cookbook like a photobook
item.description: Cooking Notes Vol. II is the second cookbook by chef Sandy Ho. Creative agency BonTemps led the creative direction and book design, with photography by Drew Escriva. The project continues a collaboration spanning Ho’s first cookbook, along with her visual identity, website and printed materials.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Latinotype’s Juana is a high-contrast serif with two partner typefaces
item.description: Juana is a serif typeface by Ely Hernández, built around contrasting thick and fine strokes, with 24 styles across two subfamilies and 130 languages. It was first published in 2020 by the independent Chilean type foundry Latinotype, which has since given the typeface a new lease of life. “This design refresh mainly involved a new set of specimen visuals that reflect how we’ve seen Juana used over the past six years,” explains Head of Digital Marketing Jorge Cisterna. “In that time, it has evolved from an editorial typeface into a corporate one, a typeface brands turn to when they want to convey elegance.” The design team adjusted sizes across the visuals to reflect that corporate work, from apps to financial brands, and made a set of animations that show Juana in the same kinds of settings.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Matey’s rebrand makes Highlands feel purposely hidden, like a rare gem
item.description: Highlands is a mountain town founded in 1875 on a plateau 4,118 feet up in North Carolina’s Blue Ridge Mountains, hours from the nearest major airport – only reachable by winding mountain roads. The Highlands Chamber of Commerce commissioned Alabama-based branding studio Matey to reposition the town and rebrand Visit Highlands, its visitor brand, so that Highlands could reclaim its own narrative. Matey was responsible for the strategy, messaging and visual identity.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Bruno’s HelloAsso identity follows France’s love of brands with values
item.description: Since 2009, HelloAsso has made life easier for non-profits across France. It is a free management platform that they use to organise events, donation drives and memberships. By acquiring tools from across the sector, it has expanded from one service into a range of solutions big enough for the largest organisations. To keep organisations as they grow, HelloAsso needed a rethink of its brand architecture – a parent brand, three offers called HelloAsso Sport, HelloAsso Generosity and HelloAsso Culture, and the HelloAsso Fund for Engagement. Global branding agency Bruno was commissioned to create HelloAsso’s strategic, verbal and visual identity, along with the web design, development, motion design, illustration and an online brand book.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: From Manchester to Apple: how Neil Nisbet learned what simple means
item.description: Neil Nisbet is a designer, creative director and musician whose work has moved between art, architecture, technology and culture for more than two decades. Through Buro Blank, his independent design practice, he works with companies in frontier technology, professional services and the built environment on identity, digital experiences and the visual expression of value. Alongside it, he maintains a music and audiovisual practice under the name Neil Blank, which acts as a creative catalyst for his commercial work. Raised outside Manchester, and now based in Los Angeles, Nisbet has built an unusually wide field of reference, from 2000 AD and Francis Bacon to Factory Records, Massimo Vignelli and Apple. We spoke about why minimalism can be sexy, how far a brand should misbehave, and why knowing where visual language has been is useful when you’re trying to work out where it might go next.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Studio Bright Green’s quietly confident identity for Levrant
item.description: London-based Studio Bright Green has created the identity for Levrant, a UK practice that works on historic buildings across architecture, heritage consultancy and townscape. Research with the practice’s team and its clients led to a name change and a visual language built around quiet confidence. That confidence runs through everything, from the typography and colour to the photography and the materials the team works with every day.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Ashfall Studio extends Carnilove’s pet food identity into a system
item.description: Carnilove is a premium pet-food brand that is sold in more than 80 markets, with an identity that Design Bridge and Partners created around the tension between the domestic pet and its wilder instincts. Prague-based design and technology partner Ashfall Studio came on board to take that identity further, spending 18 months developing it into a system for Carnilove’s teams to use across all of those markets.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: How New Apology branded ET AL for creators without factory contact
item.description: ET AL produces apparel for creative people, young clothing brands and small teams, taking on sourcing, sampling, production and delivery, as well as inventory and reorders after launch. Its customers have had to choose between print-on-demand, which is easy but generic, and traditional production, with its high minimums and months spent chasing factories. Provo-based design studio New Apology was brought in to create ET AL’s brand strategy, identity and website, as well as to art-direct all of its photography. “Together, we rallied around the concept of ‘pre-commerce’ and the thesis that ‘taste deserves infrastructure,’” explains New Apology’s founder Lyman Ballif. “Fashion and apparel production are notoriously gatekept industries where access usually requires decades of supply-chain networking. If ET AL is democratising that access, the brand needs to feel just as approachable to a creator in Des Moines, Iowa, as it does to an insider in New York.”
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Why do brand guidelines written for people fall short for AI agents?
item.description: What happens to a brand once AI agents start producing work alongside people, and where does it go wrong? Frontify, the brand intelligence tool for guidelines, assets and knowledge, has dozens of conversations every week with companies about the problems they are facing. “Everybody’s kind of going through roughly the same thing, but they just don’t speak to each other,” Senior Creative Director Hugo Timm, a Brazilian-British designer who has led Frontify’s in-house studio since 2024, tells us. “Teams really want help with automation,” he explains. “A lot of times, they’re facing pressure from above to become more efficient, or to distribute the tools to other teams, and they’re not entirely sure how to find their way towards agentic production.”
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Twice Shy positions Tula Louise as a soap atelier through a rebrand
item.description: Tula Louise is a soap brand that Jowanda Daley-Thomas started during COVID, when she began experimenting with natural pigments. Independent branding studio Twice Shy was commissioned to rework the brand as it stood, from strategy and positioning to the identity, logo, art direction and packaging design.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: A sub-45-minute 10K gave Tinloof the concept for Enroute’s identity
item.description: Enroute is a running/cycling store and community based in Vancouver that had gone for years without a clearly defined identity. With plans to grow beyond Canada, new retail stores and its first mobile app ahead, Enroute commissioned design and development agency Tinloof to create its first proper brand strategy, visual and motion identity, online store and app design. Tinloof added a watch app, too. “We needed a clear identity to root ourselves in,” explains Enroute’s founder, Sebastian Salas, a former professional athlete. “This would allow us to move confidently and create one Enroute experience across physical and online stores.”
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Jan Eumann on why Koto Berlin won’t stamp “a Koto look onto everything”
item.description: Koto is moving its Berlin operation into a studio with a lot more space – enough to double the size of its team. Executive Creative Director Jan Eumann joined from Wolff Olins as part of that expansion, arriving back in Germany after more than 12 years working in branding in the US. The studio now has 20 people from nine nationalities, many of whom moved to Berlin to work there. Eumann sees “a huge opportunity in Germany and the wider German-speaking market” and a chance to help US companies “find their feet in Europe.” In this interview, he talks to us about the studio’s push further into digital and campaigns, why it is “not interested in stamping a Koto look onto everything” and why “bigger only matters if the work gets better, too.”
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: Survive the fiscal year in Better Half / Cult Holdings’ game for Brex
item.description: Fiscal Mania is an original arcade game in which players have to survive a fiscal year. New York-based creative studio Better Half / Cult Holdings created it for Brex, a finance platform for growing companies, along with the arcade cabinets that house it, a microsite and launch events in New York and San Francisco.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity

item.title: How Afternow put Kinetik’s identity and four products into one system
item.description: Kinetik is a healthcare transportation platform that gets members to their appointments, working with health plans, brokers and transportation providers. Croatian agency Afternow has worked with Kinetik for four years, leading its rebrand, redesigning its website twice and rebuilding the design system behind four of its products.
item.dc:creator: The Brand Identity
